title: Synonyms & Antonyms: Vocabulary, Context and Exam Practice
description: High-frequency vocabulary, exact vs near-synonyms, gradable aur complementary antonyms, sentence context inference, intensity aur shades of meaning, formal vs informal register, prefix clues, word-family parts of speech, polysemy traps, aur competitive exam elimination strategies ko master karein.
learningObjectives: Synonyms aur antonyms ke precise linguistic meaning aur difference ko accurately define karein
Samajhein ki dictionary synonyms identical nahi hote aur har sentence context mein interchangeable nahi hote
Sentence ke surrounding context aur syntactic role ke hisaab se sabse appropriate synonym select karein
Direct, gradable, complementary, relational, aur context-dependent antonyms mein distinguish karein
Shades of meaning, intensity levels (annoyed vs furious), aur evaluative tone (economical vs cheap) ko pehchanein
Surrounding sentence context aur collocations ka use karke unfamiliar words ka meaning infer karein
Word families (Noun, Verb, Adjective, Adverb) ko recognize karein aur wrong grammatical roles ko eliminate karein
Common negative prefixes (un-, in-, im-, dis-, mis-) ko supporting clues ki tarah use karein aur unke limitations ko samjhein
Polysemy (multiple meanings wale words jaise sound, grave, plain, fine, sharp) ke context-specific opposites choose karein
Rajasthan High Court exams ke recurring vocabulary traps (near-synonym distractors, lookalikes, wrong intensity) ko eliminate karein
8-step exam-solving strategy apply karke vocabulary MCQs mein 100% accuracy hasil karein

included: Exact vs Near-Synonyms: Register, intensity, connotation aur collocation constraints
Antonym Typology: Gradable (polar opposites on scale), Complementary (binary either/or), Relational (converse roles), aur Contextual
Semantic Intensity Gradients: Scales of anger, size, praise, risk, speed
Contextual Sense Freezing: Word meaning locked by sentence syntax and thematic domain
Prefix Polarity Mechanics: Phonetic rules (in-, im-, il-, ir-) aur false-friend exceptions
Word Family Concord: Matching identical part-of-speech (Noun-Noun, Verb-Verb, Adj-Adj)
Polysemy Branching: Resolving multiple senses (sound, grave, plain, sharp, fine, critical)
Rajasthan High Court Legal & Administrative Lexicon: High-frequency exam terms
5-Step Cognitive MCQ Elimination Workflow: POS -> Context Sense -> Connotation -> Intensity -> Collocation
excluded: Idioms and Phrasal Verbs (Reserved for Lesson 18)
Morphological Affix Conversion Tables (Reserved for Lesson 17)
Foreign Legal Maxims in Latin (Reserved for Advanced Legal English Module)
